text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Finance Ministry to inject four billion francs into ailing Credit Lyonnais bank while it waits for European Commission to approve a new bailout plan. Publication of first-half results has been postponed one week to Oct 3. (Les Echos, La Tribune, l'Agefi, Le Figaro, Liberation). LES ECHOS
-- Paris mayor Jean Tiberis worries in an interview over the diminishing number of jobs in the capital, says town is to sell housing stock.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe has called for a parliamentary confidence vote next week.
-- Danone and Coca-Cola create joint venture in chillled fruit juice, to be called Minute Maid Danone, aims to sell to 50 countries worldwide.

-- Emmanuel Hau, a managing director at EDF electricity utility, starts legal action against chairman and former Economy Minister Edmond Alphandery who made his post redundant in a move to tighten decision-making.
-- Health Minister Jacques Barrot to call for generic drugs to be prescribed instead of more expensive, brandname products.
-- Computer group Digital Equipment Corp to shed 800 jobs in France, restructure and turn away from computer services and maintenance sectors.

-- Former Nuclear Energy Commission chairman Philippe Rouvillois allegedly wrote to President Jacques Chirac on July 5 to review possible solutions for planned merger of GEC-Alsthom with nuclear plant maker Framatome in the light of the privatisation of Thomson . Alcatel Alsthom is a bidder in the Thomson sale.
-- EU authorities to grant a further 3.2 billion francs aid package to cattle farmers hit by the BSE "mad cow" crisis.
-- In giant step, Britain, China, France, Russia and United States sign agreement to ban nuclear tests.
